chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Nothing makes wudu (ablution) obligatory except feces, or urine, or a passing of wind whose sound you hear, or a silent breaking of wind whose smell you perceive.

key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine; urination as a nullifier of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.غَائِطٌ: feces; defecation as a nullifier of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَسْوَةٌ: a passing of wind identified by its smell
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: What things make wudu (ablution) obligatory according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the events that obligate wudu (ablution), identifying specific bodily discharges that invalidate ritual purity. It is significant in fiqh because it defines key nullifiers of wudu (ablution) in a clear and practical manner for acts of worship.
